Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: ANSICE can refer violations to judicial authorities. Criminal Code (Act 001/PR/2017) includes sanctions for data protection breaches. No ID-specific judicial mechanisms identified beyond general courts.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World (checked 2026) shows ANSICE (established under Act 006/PR/2015) must inform judicial authorities of offences it detects, and a judge may impose criminal sanctions under Article 438 of the Criminal Code (Act 001/PR/2017), but no ID-specific judicial review mechanism exists beyond ordinary courts. Score of 2 ('Yes, but not specific to ID') confirmed on authoritative source, corroborating the single original citation.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: National ID card officially costs 10,000 CFA francs (~US$17). Informal payments reportedly higher. Card is not free.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original code (2='Yes', i.e. free) contradicted its own comment, which states the card costs 10,000 CFA — an internal inconsistency in the source row. Fresh reporting confirms the card is not free: the fee was cut to 5,000 CFA in Jan 2020, made temporarily free from Dec 2022, then paid again from 3 Aug 2023 (Tchadinfos), and in June 2024 the government announced a 50% discount for students/disabled (5,000 to 2,500 CFA), confirming a standard 5,000 CFA fee still applies. Recoded to 1 ('No', not free of charge).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Chad is member of CEMAC (Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa) which requires biometric identity documents per ICAO standards. Chadian national ID card recognized for travel within CEMAC region. No formal digital interoperability treaty identified.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Chad is a CEMAC member; the 2013 Additional Act abolishing visas for CEMAC nationals and CEMAC's 2019 Additional Act on common immigration policy both allow free movement for holders of a valid biometric passport or national identity card. No formal cross-border digital-ID interoperability treaty was found, so 'recognised in some regional contexts' (code 2) is confirmed rather than 'formally interoperable' (code 3). Note the comment cites ECOWAS as the illustrative example text in the scale label, but the actual regional bloc relevant to Chad is CEMAC — this is a labelling artefact, not a factual error in the score.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Wikipedia lists Chad national identity card as 'Compulsory with a price of 10,000 CFA'. Mandatory for all eligible citizens.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was Wikipedia alone (weak/aggregator). Verified against the primary legal text: the 2020 Ordonnance portant organisation de l'état civil en République du Tchad, Article 2, states that 'Toute personne résidente ou de passage au Tchad doit se faire enrôler dans le Registre National Biométrique des Populations' — enrolment in the biometric population register (which underlies national ID/NNI issuance) is compulsory for all residents, and even visitors. Code 3 ('Mandatory for all') confirmed on a stronger legal basis than the original single source.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Chad legally requires SIM card registration with national ID or passport. Telecom operators must maintain customer identification databases and provide government access. Registration with valid ID is mandatory.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source (pikasim.com, a commercial eSIM retailer) was weak and unrelated to regulation; replaced with authoritative sources. CIPESA's State of Internet Freedom in Chad report confirms the 2014 eCommunications Act and Law 014/PR/2014/Order 040/MPTIC/10 made SIM registration with an identity document compulsory, with fines for non-compliance; ARCEP inspections of Moov Africa and Airtel (May 2025) and a June 2025 crackdown on unregistered/illicit SIM kiosks (Telecompaper) confirm ongoing active enforcement. Code 3 ('Mandatory') confirmed.
